title: Canonical filtered density of accessible presentable objects
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; all smallness is relative to it and all categories have small Hom sets. Colimits have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. An infinite cardinal $\eta$ is regular when unions of fewer than $\eta$ sets each of size less than $\eta$ have size less than $\eta$. A category is $\eta$-filtered when every diagram with fewer than $\eta$ morphisms has a cocone. An object is $\eta$-presentable when its Hom functor preserves small $\eta$-filtered colimits. A category is $\eta$-accessible when it admits these colimits and has a small family of $\eta$-presentable objects generating it under these colimits; accessible means $\eta$-accessible for some infinite regular $\eta$. A functor is accessible when it preserves small $\eta$-filtered colimits for some such $\eta$ for which its source has these colimits.

Let $\mathcal A$ be $\kappa$-accessible for an infinite regular $\kappa$. Let $\mathcal P$ be its full subcategory of $\kappa$-presentable objects, and let $X\in\mathcal A$. The category $\mathcal P/X$ has objects arrows $p:P\to X$ with $P\in\mathcal P$ and morphisms $f:(P,p)\to(Q,q)$ satisfying $qf=p$. Then $\mathcal P/X$ is $\kappa$-filtered. The canonical cocone from the diagram $(P,p)\mapsto P$ to $X$, with components $p$, is colimiting. These assertions are about this explicitly specified cocone, with no assumption that $\mathcal A$ is cocomplete.
